answer: Dynamic opportunity-cost bonds lock staking collateral and impose a rising cost, deterring cheap identity replication. A subgame-perfect punishment matrix couples slashing penalties with a zero-knowledge verifiable delay, so any Sybil multiplication triggers instant forfeiture before the attacker can wander the orchard of profit. The resulting expected utility is strictly negative, placing the zenith of the attacker's payoff below zero and yielding a strict Nash equilibrium.
